name: registration number
issuer: the State Center for Civil Registration and Information (SCCRI), as the source of 2012 names it
note: Landinfo's thematic note on Mongolia's travel, identity and supporting documents (22 November 2012), read 2026-10-30, citing a meeting with the SCCRI in Ulaanbaatar (May 2012) and a Mongolian diplomat (October 2011): the national register is kept by the SCCRI; ID cards, old and new, carry a document number and a registration number; the registration number, comparable to Norway's personal number, is given to every Mongolian citizen at birth and follows them for life; it is made of two letters and eight digits, from which the authorities read sex, date and place of birth. The note doesn't say which alphabet the two letters are in, so the pattern takes any Latin or Cyrillic letter (a superset; Mongolian is written in Cyrillic, which the source doesn't state). Read as given at birth, to citizens. The note is of 2012 (the register's office has since been reorganised; its current site burtgel.gov.mn answers but no page stating the number's form was found today; legalinfo.mn didn't answer). No check digit, fee or time is stated.

sources.title: Landinfo (the Norwegian immigration authorities' country-information centre), Temanotat Mongolia: Reise-, ID- og underlagsdokumenter, 22 November 2012
sources.said: The Mongolian national register is administered by the State Center for Civil Registration and Information (SCCRI). ... Både de tidligere og de nye ID-kortene utstedes av SCCRI, og har to tallrekker ... ettersom det tildeles alle mongolske borgere ved fødselen og følger dem gjennom hele livet ... Reigstreringsnummeret består av to bokstaver og åtte siffer
